issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): the UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md line 72) declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() to return a double, but the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 85) defines the method as returning an int (public int getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()). This both changes the numeric semantics (integer division vs. floating-point division) and contradicts the UML, which can confuse students and may cause tests that expect a double result to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the UML by changing the method signature to return double in both solution and template: public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(). Implement the calculation using floating-point division to preserve fractional students-per-tutor, for example: return getTotalNumberOfStudents() / (double) getNumberOfTutors();. Update the template's TODO or method stub to indicate a double return type so students implement the correct signature, and adjust any tests or documentation that assume this method returns an int.
